newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan approves gene therapy for HIV patients.
newsitem.headline: Japan approves gene therapy for HIV patients.

text.p: Japan's Health Ministry said on Monday it has given the go-ahead for clinical trials of a gene therapy for patients with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.
It will be the first time in Japan that HIV patients receive gene therapy, the ministry said. Currently, there are 4,088 HIV patients in Japan, according to the latest ministry data.
The trial will include four HIV patients at Kumamoto University in southern Japan and will be sponsored by Osaka-based drug maker Green Cross Corp.

The gene therapy, already undergoing clinical tests on a much larger scale in the United States, injects patients with genes encoding certain HIV proteins and stimulates their immune systems to attack the virus.
The therapy utilises HIV-IT(V), a drug under development by a division of U.S.-based Chiron Corp.
Green Cross said in February it would spend an additional $4 million this year to expand human clinical studies of the immunotherapeutic HIV drug.
Under an agreement between the two companies, Chiron is in charge of research and development of the drug and will be responsible for manufacturing, while Green Cross has worldwide marketing rights.
Japanese media reports said the clinical trial at Kumamoto University is expected to begin as early as July.
The trial comes at a time when Green Cross is still reeling from a scandal surrounding HIV-tainted blood products.

Former Green Cross executives were indicted last October on charges of professional negligence for selling blood products that could infect patients with HIV. The products were not heat-treated, even though company documents showed that officials knew untreated products posed a risk of HIV infection.
The company also faces compensation payments totalling approximately 24 billion yen ($206 million) to haemophiliacs who were infected by the products.

Green Cross is scheduled to merge into another Osaka-based drug company, Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd, on April 1, 1998. The date of the merger was postponed last month from the original target of October 1.
